transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My team keeps telling me my behavior and decisions don’t make sense anymore, and I feel like I can’t control what I’m doing at work. It has gotten to the point where my board and my spouse are really alarmed, and I just don't know how to handle it anymore.
Have you ever had a similar period before where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or made impulsive decisions?

No, I've never really had periods where I felt unusually energized or didn't need sleep. If anything, it’s the complete opposite lately—I just feel incredibly flat, drained, and unable to organize my thoughts or actions at all.

Have you often found it hard to care about other people’s feelings or to feel guilt after hurting or taking advantage of someone? Do you usually blame others instead of taking responsibility when your actions cause problems?

No, I don't relate to that at all. I would never try to take advantage of or hurt anyone, and I don't blame others for my mistakes. I just feel incredibly disconnected, flat, and completely confused by my own behavior lately.
How much have these symptoms affected your ability to work, take care of yourself, and do everyday activities? Have you been able to function at all, or has it become nearly impossible?

It has become nearly impossible for me to function lately. I went from reliably running my company and art projects to missing critical meetings and almost losing a major client, leading my spouse and board to question if I can even continue in my role. I've also completely pulled away from friends and have been neglecting basic daily routines like showering.
Have you been having thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had thoughts of hurting myself or felt like life isn't worth living. I just feel incredibly flat, empty, and detached from everything right now. It's more like my mind and emotions have just completely shut off.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or have you had strong beliefs that others say are not true, such as feeling watched, controlled, or blamed without reason?

Yes, for about the last three months, I've regularly heard a man's voice, very clear like someone on a conference call without video, commenting on what I'm doing. He tells me that I'm making a mess of the company or that people are laughing at me, even when I'm completely alone in my apartment or a quiet boardroom. It's incredibly unsettling because I know there is no one actually there talking.
Have you also had any fixed beliefs that other people say are not true, such as feeling watched, controlled, or that your thoughts are being broadcast or inserted into your mind?
No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of fixed beliefs. I don't feel like I'm being watched, and I've never felt like my thoughts are being broadcast or inserted into my mind.
Have these voices been present even when your mood is at its worst, or do they only happen during times when you feel especially depressed and slowed down?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether there is a connection between my mood and when I hear the voice. It just seems to happen, regardless of how flat or drained I am feeling.
When you hear the voice, does it only happen during your worst depressive periods, or has it also been present at times when your mood felt more normal?
I'm really not sure. I haven't noticed any connection between my mood and when the voice appears. It just seems to happen regardless of whether I'm feeling completely flat or relatively normal.
Have you ever had similar episodes of depression before this one, lasting at least two weeks and causing a major drop in your work or daily functioning?

No, I've never experienced distinct, severe episodes of depression like that in the past. Before these recent struggles started, I was always able to manage my work and daily life quite well without those kinds of periods.
Do the voice and other unusual experiences ever continue when your mood is not depressed, or do they only happen during the times when you feel most flat and low?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it that way. Everything has felt so overwhelming and jumbled together lately that it's hard to tell if they happen separately or together. It all just feels like one big, confusing blur.
Have there been any times in the last few months when your mood felt more normal or less depressed, but you were still hearing the voice?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I mostly just feel flat or empty all the time anyway, so I haven't really noticed my mood changing. The voice just seems to be there regardless.
Have you had any periods of at least a few days when your mood felt more normal or less depressed, but you were still hearing the voice?

I'm really not sure about that. I haven't noticed any periods where my mood felt more normal because I've just felt so flat and blank lately. The voice just seems to happen without any real connection to how I'm feeling.
Have the voice and any other unusual experiences continued even when your depression was not at its worst, or do they only happen during the times when you feel most depressed?

I'm not really sure how to relate this to depression because I don't experience distinct ups and downs—it has just been a constant flatness lately. The voice has simply been a regular, ongoing presence for the last three months regardless of my mood.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when your mood was not depressed but you were still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?
I'm really not sure about that. I haven't thought about my mood in relation to the voice in that specific way, especially since everything has just felt like a constant, flat blur lately.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when your mood was not depressed, but you were still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?

Yes, I've been hearing that voice regularly for about the last three months now. During this time, I wouldn't really describe my mood as deeply depressed, but rather just completely flat, blank, and empty inside. The voice persists constantly, regardless of my emotional state.
Have you noticed any other psychotic symptoms, such as feeling that people are watching you, that your thoughts are being controlled or inserted, or that you have a special mission or unusual powers?
No, I haven't experienced any of those feelings. I don't feel like people are watching me, that my thoughts are being controlled, or that I have any kind of special mission or unusual powers.
Have you had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt clearly depressed or lost interest in things, while the voice was still present even though your mood was otherwise not depressed?

I have definitely lost interest in almost everything and felt completely flat and blank for a long time now, rather than feeling actively sad or depressed. Meanwhile, the voice has been a regular, clear presence for the past three months, and it occurs constantly regardless of how empty or flat I am feeling at any given moment.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were clearly depressed or lost interest in things, but the voice was still present even when your mood was otherwise not depressed?

I don't really experience typical depression or sadness, but rather a constant flatness and lack of motivation. Because of that, I'm really not sure how to distinguish the timing of these feelings from when I hear the voice. They both just feel like they are constantly there.
Have you ever had a clear period of at least two weeks when your mood was normal or only mildly low, but you were still hearing the voice?
I'm not really sure, it's hard to separate my mood from everything else going on. The voice has just been a constant presence lately, regardless of how I'm feeling.
Have the voice and other unusual experiences ever continued for at least two weeks when you were not feeling depressed or emotionally flat?

I'm not quite sure because I find it really hard to distinguish between them. The flat, blank feelings and the voices have both been happening around the same time over the last few months, so I can't easily separate them. I don't recall any specific two-week period where I felt completely normal emotionally but still heard the voices.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when your mood was back to normal or only mildly low, but you were still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?

I'm really not sure about my mood returning to normal, because I have mostly just felt consistently flat, blank, and disconnected lately. The voices and strange experiences have just been happening regularly for the last three months regardless of how I feel.
Have you ever had a clear period of at least 2 weeks when your mood felt normal or only mildly low, but you were still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?

I honestly can't say, because I haven't had a period where my mood felt normal in a very long time. I've just felt consistently flat and blank lately, so it's hard to separate my mood from the voices. They both just seem to be there together.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when your mood felt normal or only mildly low, but you were still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?

I’m really not sure, as I haven't tracked my mood in relation to the voices that way. Everything has just felt like a constant, flat blur for so long that I can't recall a time when my mood felt normal for two weeks.
Have you noticed that the voice and other unusual experiences started before your low mood and flatness, or did they begin only after the mood symptoms began?

The flatness, lack of motivation, and withdrawal actually started first, about two years ago around the time of that big merger project. The clear voice and the bizarre behaviors at work are much more recent, only becoming a regular problem over the last three months.
Have the voices or any other unusual experiences ever started before your flat or depressed mood began, or have they only appeared after the mood symptoms started?
They definitely appeared after the flatness started. The flat, blank feeling and lack of motivation began about two years ago during the merger, while the voice only started about three months ago.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when your mood felt normal or only mildly low, but you were still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?

I'm not really sure about that. My mood has just felt consistently flat and empty lately, rather than having distinct phases where things felt normal. The voices just seem to happen alongside this constant flatness.
Have the voices ever continued for at least 2 weeks during a time when you felt emotionally normal or only mildly low, rather than flat or depressed?

I'm not quite sure, as I haven't tracked the timing that closely. I've felt so flat and detached for such a long time now that it's hard to even remember a period of feeling completely normal while hearing the voices.
Have you ever had a clear period of at least 2 weeks when you felt emotionally normal or only mildly low, while still hearing the voice or having other unusual experiences?

I'm really not sure, and I haven't really thought about it that way. My feelings have mostly just been flat and blank lately while the voices have been happening. Because of that, I can't recall a specific two-week period where my mood was normal while still hearing them.
Have the voices ever continued for at least 2 weeks during a time when you felt emotionally normal or only mildly low, rather than flat or depressed?

I'm really not sure because I haven't tracked the exact timing of my flat feelings compared to when the voices started. Everything has felt quite overwhelming and blurry over the last few months, so it's hard to say.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear psychotic symptom (persistent auditory hallucinations for 3 months) together with prominent long-standing depressive/negative symptoms (flatness, anhedonia, avolition, social withdrawal, poor self-care, impaired work functioning). This pattern is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type rather than schizophrenia alone.
